subject: robinhood

error_analyses.observable_characteristics: The supplied KFG marks the email input as both v_0 and v_entry, indicating the form's implemented tab entry point is the email field. However, the same KFG also contains v_exit ENTER to the forgot-password link, and the ground truth labels Browser -> forgot-password link as an LNF. In the screenshot, the forgot-password link is visually below the password field and above the Sign In button, not the first form control in the visible top-to-bottom sequence. Navigation_order places this link at meaningful position 4 but implemented label 1.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A transition matches this pattern when the source is the virtual Browser boundary, the destination is the first implemented focus target, and that destination is a lower or later page control rather than the visually/semantically first control in the form or task sequence.
error_analyses.possible_cause: Observed evidence shows a browser-boundary LNF exists in ground truth but was absent from original_predictions. A plausible hypothesis is that the original detector under-modeled or filtered Browser boundary transitions, or prioritized only intra-page element-to-element anomalies. This is unverified because the detector's internal rules are not provided.
error_analyses.supporting_evidence: ground_truth includes "Browser -> /html[1]/body[1]/div[1]/div[1]/div[2]/div[1]/div[1]/div[1]/div[1]/div[1]/form[1]/div[1]/p[1]/a[1]"; evaluated_transitions classifies it as FN with browser_boundary="True" and observed_in_stage1="True"; navigation_order shows the destination link has position 4 and label 1; kfg v_special shows v_0 and v_entry at the email input, while kfg v_exit lists ENTER to the forgot-password link; screenshot annotation places marker 1 on the forgot-password link below markers 2, 3, and 4.

correct_transition_examples.relevant_characteristic: Useful comparison because it is the companion intra-page wrap from the same misplaced first focus target back to the top email input, showing the detector did catch the non-browser version of the same ordering anomaly.
Shows ordinary forward movement between the first two text fields in the expected form sequence.
Shows expected local progression within the password field group to its adjacent show/hide control.
Shows that not every inferred-position gap is treated as an LNF; despite bypassing the forgot-password link in meaningful-position numbering, this implemented move was not labeled a failure.

subject_summary: This subject shows a login form whose implemented focus order begins on the forgot-password link rather than the email field, creating both a browser-entry anomaly and an intra-page wrap back to the top input. The detector correctly reported the intra-page link-to-email transition but missed the Browser boundary transition to the same misplaced starting element. Evidence supports a likely browser-boundary handling gap, though the detector's internal mechanism is not directly observable.
